title: Unify credential contracts, add concrete streaming examples, and sync SDK versions
author: Anika Rao
description: Motivation: multiple SDKs exposed subtly different credential shapes and streaming helpers which caused confusion in downstream platform code and in customer integrations. This PR introduces a small, explicit CredentialContract surface and three concrete, idiomatic streaming examples (Python async iterator, TypeScript async generator, Go channel-based iterator). The goal is ergonomics parity across SDKs while keeping the runtime backoff behavior unchanged. Changes include: extraction of a CredentialContract interface, adapter shims for legacy credential providers, a cross-sdk parity test harness, updated docs with copy-paste ready examples, and coordinated SDK version bumps. Checklist: - [x] Define CredentialContract and document expected behaviors (sync/async, heartbeats) - [x] Implement adapters in py/ts/go to present a consistent API - [x] Add unit + integration parity tests that exercise token refresh, reauth race, and abort semantics - [x] Update examples in docs site and README snippets - [x] Bump SDK minors to 1.21.0 (py/ts/go) - [x] Run CI and address lint/test failures Notes & links: design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/notes/ENG-1248/credential-contract-and-stream-examples; staging integration run: pipeline/infra-e2e/245. Backwards compatibility: legacy credential providers are supported via small adapter shims included in this change. No breaking changes expected for consumers that use official SDKs as shipped, but custom credential implementations that relied on an internal shape may need a one-line adapter. Test plan: cross-sdk parity harness (tests/parity/) runs the same scripted scenarios against each SDK in a containerized environment; added scenarios for rapid token expiry and network interruptions. Deployment: merged to main; no rollout gating required for hosted API surface changes, this affects SDK consumers only.
